sentences.text: Sheshnath Sharma vs Sunidhi Sharma on 23 February, 2026

In The Supreme Court Of India
 Civil Appellate Jurisdiction
 Civil Appeal No. 2443 Of 2026
 (@ Special Leave Petition (Civil) No. 23447/2025)
 Sheshnath Sharma 
 Versus
 Sunidhi Sharma & Anr. 
 O R D E R
1. Heard learned counsel for the parties.

2. Leave granted.
3.
By an order dated 29.08.2025, the parties were referred for mediation before the Coordinator of the Supreme Court Mediation Centre.
4. The parties have arrived at a settlement and the Settlement dated 03.12.2025 is placed on record.
5. An application seeking dissolution of marriage dated 28.11.2016 by a decree of divorce on the basis of mutual consent has been filed under Article 142 of the Constitution of India.
6. In the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case, we consider it appropriate to exercise our discretionary jurisdiction under Article 142 of the Constitution of India.
Reason: 7.
The application is allowed and the marriage between the parties is dissolved in terms of the settlement dated 03.12.2025.
The settlement dated 03.12.2025 is annexed to this Order, and read together with this Order for all purposes.
8. It is needless to observe that the pending litigation between the parties is also either terminated or wound up by the respective courts as has been agreed between the parties.
9. The appeal shall stand disposed of in terms of the Settlement Agreement.
The parties shall remain bound by the terms and conditions of the Settlement Agreement.

NEW DELHI 23rd February, 2026.
GA SETTLEMENT AGREEMENT This Settlement Agreement is entered into between Petitioner  Mr. Sheshnath Sharma S/o Late Krishna Nand Sharma, R/o Section-II/D, Street-5, QRS No. 1-278,
P.O., P.S.-B.S. City Bokaro, Jharkhand (hereinafter referred to as Petitioner-Husband) and Ms.
Sunidhi Sharma D/o Mr. Surendra Sharma W/o Sheshnath Sharma R/o Section-II/B, QRS No.
3-127, P.O., P.S.-B.S. City Bokaro, Jharkhand (hereinafter referred to as Respondent/Wife).
1. Whereas the marriage between the petitioner and respondent/wife was solemnized as per Hindu rites and ceremonies on 28.11.2016 at Bokaro, Steel City, Jharkhand.
After marriage parties resided together at Bangalore and there is no issue out of wedlock.

2. Both the parties resided together as husband and wife till 02.08.2018, and thereafter disputes and differences arose between the parties and since then Respondent/wife is staying with her parents at Bokaro, Jharkhand.
The Petitioner/Husband has filed Original Suit No. 522/2019 before the Family Court at Bokaro seeking dissolution of marriage.

3. Whereas the Parties have filed following cases against each other:-
(i) The Petitioner/Husband has filed Original Suit No. 522/2019 before the Family Court at Bokaro.

(ii) The Respondent/Wife has filed Complaint Case No. 834/2018 under Section 498A IPC r/w Section 3 & 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, titled as Sunidhi Sharma Vs Sheshnath Sharma and Ors., pending before Ld. CJM, Bokaro- Jharkhand.

Comprehensive mediation sessions were held between the parties and their respective advocates on 04.09.2025, 03.10.2025,
07.10.2025, 10.10.2025 by both physical and virtual mode and finally on 03.12.2025 parties have arrived to settle the dispute.

5. Both the parties hereto have arrived at an amicable settlement on the following terms and conditions for dissolution of marriage by mutual consent:-

sentences.text:
The parties have agreed that the Petitioner- husband will pay to the Respondent/Wife a total sum of Rs. 18,50,000/- (Rupees Eighteen Lakhs and Fifty Thousand Only) towards full and final settlement of all her claims towards her permanent alimony, Stridhan, maintenance (past, present,
future) and any other claim whatsoever.
B.

It is agreed between the parties that they will move an application jointly before the Honble Supreme Court under Article 142 of the Constitution of India for invoking inherent powers of the Honble Supreme Court praying for divorce by mutual consent as parties are staying separately since 02.08.2018 i.e. for the last more than seven years and there is irretrievable breakdown of the marriage.

C. It is further agreed between the parties that on allowing the applications made by both the parties for dissolution of marriage under Article 142 of the Constitution of India,
by the Honble Supreme Court of India.
The parties shall withdraw all the cases filed by them against each other.

The Petitioner- husband will pay to the Respondent/Wife a total sum of Rs. 18,50,000/- (Rupees Eighteen Lakhs and Fifty Thousand Only) via RTGS/NEFT/Online Transfer in the account bearing No. 38923813858, SBI,
Sector-I, Bokaro, Steel City, IFSC SBIN0007872.

AND/OR The Petitioner-husband will pay an amount of Rs. 18,50,000/- (Rupees Eighteen Lakhs and Fifty Thousand Only) in 2 installments as under:-
I.

The Petitioner-husband shall pay first installment an amount of Rs. 5,00,000/-
 (Rupees Five Lakhs Only) in favour of the  Respondent No.1/Wife by way of  RTGS/NEFT/Online Payment at the time of signing of this present Settlement Agreement.

II. The Petitioner-husband shall pay second installment an amount of Rs. 13,50,000/- (Rupees Thirteen Lakhs and Fifty Thousand Only) in favour of the Respondent No.1/Wife by way of RTGS/NEFT/Online Payment on or before 20th December 2025.

6. The Petitioner and the Respondent have agreed that none of them will initiate any other legal action or complaint against each other or against the family members of each other in respect of their matrimonial dispute in future.

7. That subject to the aforesaid terms, the parties have resolved all the disputes amicably in relation to the marriage and have been left with no claims against each other or their respective family members.

8. That by signing this Agreement the parties hereto solemnly state and affirm that they have no further claims or demands against each other including maintenance, or any movable or immovable property and all the disputes and differences have been amicably settled by the parties hereto Sheshnath Sharma vs Sunidhi Sharma on 23 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103365320/
3 through the process of mediation.

9. The parties undertake to abide by the terms and conditions set out in the above mentioned Settlement Agreement, which have been arrived with free will of the parties without any coercion,
duress or collusion and parties undertake not to raise any dispute whatsoever henceforth.
10. The contents of this settlement agreement have been explained to all the parties through their respective counsels and they have understood the same.
